questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid quoting a specific AI engineering salary figure?
options: Because salary figures go stale fast and vary too much by location, company stage, and role to verify as current for any one learner
Because AI engineers are never paid a salary, only equity
Because the lesson considers compensation an inappropriate topic to discuss at all
Because every AI engineering job pays exactly the same amount worldwide
questions.explain: The lesson explains that salary numbers age quickly and vary by market, so it teaches a research process instead of quoting a figure that could already be wrong.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why do AI engineering job titles vary so widely in what they actually mean?
options: Because titles like 'AI Engineer,' 'Machine Learning Engineer,' and 'Applied AI Engineer' can describe nearly identical work at one company or very different scopes at another
Because every company is legally required to use a different title
Because AI engineering titles are standardized by a single global authority
Because job titles have no connection to actual responsibilities in any field
questions.explain: The lesson warns that unstandardized titles can hide very different actual responsibilities, so reading the posting's real duties matters more than the title alone.

questions.q: Which combination of source types does the lesson recommend for building a realistic compensation range?
options: A single number remembered from a friend's conversation
Only the first search result from a general web search
Aggregated salary sites, government labor data, and live job postings, from at least two independent sources
Whatever number appears first on a social media post
questions.explain: The lesson's research toolkit table lists aggregated salary sites, government labor data, and live postings, and instructs building a range from at least two independent sources.

questions.q: When evaluating a real job offer, what does the lesson say to look at beyond the headline base salary number?
options: Nothing else matters besides the base number
Only the company's stock ticker symbol
The whole package: base, equity and its vesting schedule, signing bonus, flexibility, and the timeline to the first compensation review
Only whether the office has free snacks
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly lists the whole compensation package -- base, equity/vesting, signing bonus, flexibility, and review timeline -- as what to evaluate, not just the base number.

questions.q: Which group of courses does this lesson's recap place together as 'building real systems' in the AI Engineer path?
options: Python, Git & GitHub, and APIs & JSON
Generative AI & LLMs, Prompt & Context Engineering, RAG & Vector Databases, and AI Agents
Azure AI & Cloud, Docker & Deployment, and AI Security, Evaluation & Monitoring
Only the Capstones course by itself
questions.explain: The lesson's recap groups Generative AI & LLMs, Prompt & Context Engineering, RAG & Vector Databases, and AI Agents together as the path's progression from understanding models to building systems that act.
